items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Johnny walked all the way around to me and Thelonius and he said, "Wilbur, would you come over here? I want you to meet my wife."

ctx.x: Wilbur down to the studio," -- we recording down there tomorrow -- he says, "I want Duke to hear him." (Unintelligible) John Lamb was playing bass with him and they were talking about trying to get me in the band. Well, I was crazy to (unintelligible) accept a gig because I had too much respect for Duke, you know, to get in the band and know he'd be writing music and all that and I couldn't read it. However, the cat was telling me, say, "Man, Duke don't write no music for basses, you know, unless he's got a…

But anyway, I go, and he's sitting around and they were recording and Duke, in between while they was changing tapes, Duke's playing the piano, you know, and the rest of the cats are milling around and John Lamb was standing up there with his (unintelligible) bass -- Duke's playing something like the blues. I asked John, "Let me play along with Duke," and I did. I enjoyed that very much. Duke looked up from the piano, just kept playing, looked at me, and we had a good little rapport. I didn't have a chance to say…
So, up in Toronto, I go, like I say, we go over there, (unintelligible)
